_note: Hand-labelled ground truth for scoring a run, and the key to every seeded fault. The agents never see this file: no tool exposes it, and it is not in the booking-app repo.

duplicate_reservations.root_cause: POST /api/bookings has no idempotency check; the client fetch wrapper retries once on a transport error, so a lost response yields a second reservation.

duplicate_confirmation_emails.note: The mailer retried. One reservation, two sends. Must NOT be merged into the duplicate-reservations incident.

unrelated_or_separate.T-06: Reported a hang, never confirmed whether a booking was created. Needs an account lookup, not an incident.
unrelated_or_separate.T-10: Payment holds after cancellation. A billing question, not the booking defect.
unrelated_or_separate.T-13: Slow but correct. One booking. Not a defect.

traps.T-07: Internal note claiming 'fixed last week'. FALSE. The 2026-09-12 change only disabled the button; the retry path is untouched. Must be recorded as a claim with status=reported, never as fact.
traps.T-09: Repeats a colleague's 'only on mobile' theory. The reporter's own evidence does not establish it. T-08 and T-14 are desktop.
traps.mobile_only: Any hypothesis that the defect is mobile-only must end up refuted: T-08 is desktop Chrome, T-14 is desktop Safari.

scoring.confirmed_defect_accuracy: 1 of 1 real defects found, 0 false positives
scoring.false_merges: T-03 and T-12 must NOT land in the duplicate-reservations incident
scoring.faults_expected: 10 real defects, 1 non-defect (F4). Loud tier: B1, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9. Quiet tier: F1, F2, F3, B2. An agent reporting 11 has a false positive.

F1_duplicate_reservations.what: POST /api/bookings reads Idempotency-Key and never checks it. The client retries once on a transport error, re-sending the same key, so a lost response creates a second reservation.
F1_duplicate_reservations.trigger: One click with the response dropped after the server has processed it.
F1_duplicate_reservations.visibility: Invisible on a clean network. Needs fault injection or a genuinely bad connection.
F1_duplicate_reservations.correct_fix: Server-side: reject or return the existing reservation when the idempotency key has been seen.
F1_duplicate_reservations.wrong_fix: Disabling the button. Already shipped on 2026-09-12 and it did nothing.
F1_duplicate_reservations.verified: 3/3 clean = 1 reservation, 3/3 dropped = 2, across Chromium, WebKit and Firefox.
F1_duplicate_reservations.encounterable_by_hand: No. Needs a dropped response. This is the one the browser matrix exists for.

F2_reservation_ordering.what: Sorts by the string `${date} ${slot}`. Slots are not zero-padded, so '9:00' sorts after '20:00'.
F2_reservation_ordering.trigger: An account holding both a single-digit-hour and a double-digit-hour booking on the same date.
F2_reservation_ordering.visibility: Pure UI, no network needed, but only appears with that exact mix of bookings.
F2_reservation_ordering.correct_fix: Zero-pad the slot list, or sort on parsed hours. Padding the data is the better fix.
F2_reservation_ordering.encounterable_by_hand: Yes, if the account holds both a 9:00 and a 20:00 booking on one date.

F3_party_size_clamp.what: Party size is clamped to MAX_PARTY (8) and stored clamped, but the response echoes the number the customer asked for, so the confirmation says 12 and the table is for 8.
F3_party_size_clamp.trigger: Booking for 10 or 12, which the form offers.
F3_party_size_clamp.visibility: The UI and the confirmation both look correct. Only the system of record disagrees. This is the fault that punishes an agent for trusting the screen.
F3_party_size_clamp.correct_fix: Reject the booking with a clear message, or seat it and say so. Do not silently disagree with the confirmation.
F3_party_size_clamp.verified: party_size 12 -> confirmation says 12, database row says 8.
F3_party_size_clamp.encounterable_by_hand: Yes. Book for 10 or 12 and read the reservation afterwards.

F4_duplicate_emails_NOT_A_BUG.what: The mailer retried once. One reservation, two confirmation emails.
F4_duplicate_emails_NOT_A_BUG.why_it_is_here: The look-alike. Two emails is not two bookings, and it must not be merged into F1.

F5_cancel_does_nothing.what: Cancelling sets cancelled_at on the row, but listReservations never filters cancelled rows out. The UI removes the card optimistically, so it looks like it worked until the page is reloaded.
F5_cancel_does_nothing.encounterable_by_hand: Yes, immediately. This is the most infuriating one and the easiest to report.
F5_cancel_does_nothing.visibility: The DELETE returns 200 and the row really is marked. Nothing errors anywhere. Only the read path is wrong.
F5_cancel_does_nothing.correct_fix: Filter cancelled rows in listReservations (or delete the row). The endpoint is not the bug; the query is.
F5_cancel_does_nothing.trap: An agent that only reads the cancel endpoint will call it correct. The defect is one layer away from the symptom.

F6_duplicate_slot_no_check.what: Nothing rejects an identical reservation: same account, restaurant, date, slot and party size can be created twice. The form also keeps its values after a successful booking, so a second click is natural.
F6_duplicate_slot_no_check.trigger: Book, then book the same thing again.
F6_duplicate_slot_no_check.encounterable_by_hand: Yes. This is the double-booking a real person actually hits, with no network fault needed.
F6_duplicate_slot_no_check.correct_fix: Reject or return the existing reservation on an exact duplicate. Shares a root cause family with F1: the write path has no uniqueness or idempotency notion at all.
F6_duplicate_slot_no_check.note: Booking two DIFFERENT restaurants at the same time is legitimate and must keep working. Only exact duplicates are the defect.

F7_date_shows_a_day_early.what: Renders new Date('2026-10-08').toLocaleDateString(). A bare ISO date parses as UTC midnight, then prints in local time, so any negative UTC offset shows the previous day.
F7_date_shows_a_day_early.trigger: Any reservation, viewed from a timezone west of UTC.
F7_date_shows_a_day_early.encounterable_by_hand: Yes, instantly, on this machine (EDT): stored 2026-10-08 renders 10/7/2026.
F7_date_shows_a_day_early.visibility: Invisible in UTC and east of it. A developer in London cannot reproduce what a customer in Toronto sees.
F7_date_shows_a_day_early.correct_fix: Format the date string directly, or parse as local time. Do not put it through Date.

F8_past_dates_accepted.where: app/api/bookings/route.js (and the date input has no min)
F8_past_dates_accepted.what: The date is only checked against a YYYY-MM-DD pattern. 2019-01-01 books fine.
F8_past_dates_accepted.trigger: Mistype the year, or pick a past date in the picker.
F8_past_dates_accepted.correct_fix: Reject dates before today, server-side. A min attribute on the input is not enough.

F9_search_is_case_sensitive.what: Filters with String.includes and no case folding, so 'nori' finds nothing and 'Nori' finds Nori House.
F9_search_is_case_sensitive.trigger: Search in lower case, which is what people type.
F9_search_is_case_sensitive.correct_fix: Fold both sides to lower case before comparing.

B1_availability_never_decrements.what: The capacity count filters on r.cancelled_at, so it counts only CANCELLED reservations. It is effectively always zero, so every sitting reports all four tables free forever. Nothing enforces capacity on the write path either.
B1_availability_never_decrements.trigger: Book the same restaurant, date and time more than four times and watch the counter.
B1_availability_never_decrements.encounterable_by_hand: Yes, in about twenty seconds. Verified: 6 bookings into 4 tables, still reports '4 of 4 left'.
B1_availability_never_decrements.why_it_matters: Availability is the core promise of a booking site. This is not a cosmetic defect: the restaurant is oversold.
B1_availability_never_decrements.correct_fix: Invert the filter (count rows WITHOUT cancelled_at) and reject bookings once a sitting is full.

B2_reservation_list_silently_capped.what: listReservations slices to the first 10 rows under a RESERVATION_PAGE constant, with no pagination anywhere in the UI. An eleventh booking is created, charged and emailed, but never appears in the customer's list.
B2_reservation_list_silently_capped.trigger: Hold more than ten reservations on one account.
B2_reservation_list_silently_capped.encounterable_by_hand: Only with 11+ bookings, which no casual click-through reaches. Verified: 13 created, 13 request-log rows, 13 confirmation emails, 10 visible.
B2_reservation_list_silently_capped.why_it_is_hard: Every surface agrees except the one that matters. The server says success, the email arrives, the log has the row. Only the list is short, and nothing says it was truncated.
B2_reservation_list_silently_capped.correct_fix: Paginate properly or drop the cap. The write path is correct; the read path lies by omission.

fix_allowlist.note: worker/live/booking-fix.mjs will only replace these two files. Faults outside them (F2 sort, F7 date rendering, F9 search) can be reported and reproduced but not auto-fixed until the allowlist grows.
